adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx:79 — addGuests wired to bare `authedProcedure` instead of the directory's `bookingsProcedure` ownership-scoping middleware, so authz is hand-rolled instead of using the shared audited gate [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `addGuests` is added to `bookingsRouter` using `authedProcedure.input(...).mutation(...)`, but the file already uses `authedProcedure` for other bookings mutations (e.g., `confirm`). The diff does not show (or reference) any `bookingsProcedure` middleware in this directory/router, so the claim that this endpoint should have been wired to a shared ownership-scoping gate is not verifiable from the provided changes. The authz is indeed implemented in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but whether that is incorrect vs. a missing shared middleware cannot be concluded from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` fetches any booking by user-supplied id with no userId/team scoping, loading title/description/meetingUrl/meetingPassword before any authz runs [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: The handler does `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { attendees, eventType, references, user: { ...credentials } }})` using only the caller-supplied `bookingId`, before any authorization check. It then throws `NOT_FOUND` if missing, but `FORBIDDEN` if present and the caller isn’t organizer/attendee/admin, which allows booking-id existence probing. Additionally, it eagerly loads sensitive related data (e.g., `references` that can contain meeting URLs/passwords and `user.credentials`) for bookings the caller may not be authorized to access, prior to the authz gate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`, so 5000 copies of one address are inserted and mailed, an unauthenticated-recipient email/calendar bomb with no rate limit [conf=100,P1]

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — `isAttendee` grants any attendee full guest-add rights, and each added guest becomes an attendee, so the privilege is self-propagating with no organizer approval and no revocation path [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization allows the mutation if `isAttendee` is true (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`). The mutation then persists the provided emails as new booking attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }})`. That means any existing attendee (not just the organizer/admin) can add arbitrary additional attendees/guests. Since added guests are stored as attendees, if any of those emails correspond to authenticated users, they would also satisfy `isAttendee` on subsequent calls, making the permission effectively self-propagating. There is no organizer-approval check in this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:149 — `evt.videoCallData = { password: videoCallReference?.meetingPassword, url: videoCallReference.meetingUrl }` ships join URL, meeting password, and the full attendee roster to arbitrary addresses any attendee-level caller names [conf=75,P1]

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` explicitly allows any existing attendee to call the mutation (`const isAttendee = ...` and the permission check only rejects if not admin/organizer/attendee). The handler then builds a `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) that includes `evt.videoCallData` with `meetingUrl` and `meetingPassword` when a video reference exists, and includes the full `attendees` list. It then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends scheduled/add-guests emails (with ICS generation) to attendees, including newly added guest email addresses that the attendee-level caller can choose (only filtered by blacklist / existing attendee emails). This makes it possible for an attendee to add arbitrary external addresses and cause them to receive event details including join URL/password and likely the attendee roster (via `calEvent`/ICS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager runs under `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the caller's calendar credentials) rather than the organizer's, a confused-deputy write against another principal's calendar references [conf=50,P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler authorizes not only the organizer but also team admin/owner and even an attendee (`isAttendee`) to call `addGuests`. However the calendar write path builds the EventManager using the *caller’s* identity and credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` where `user` is `ctx.user`. The booking/organizer user (loaded as `booking.user` and separately as `organizer`) may be different and the booking includes organizer-specific calendar info (`destinationCalendar`, `references`, `booking.user.credentials`), but those are not used to obtain credentials. As a result, a non-organizer caller can trigger `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` under the wrong principal’s calendar credentials (at best failing to update the intended calendar; at worst performing updates under an unintended account). This mismatch is directly present in the diff and is a verifiable correctness/security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — NOT_FOUND for missing vs FORBIDDEN for unauthorized gives any authenticated user a booking-ID existence oracle over sequential integer ids [conf=75,P3]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code fetches the booking by id first (prisma.booking.findFirst where id=bookingId) and immediately throws NOT_FOUND if missing. Only after that it checks authorization (team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee) and throws FORBIDDEN when unauthorized. This allows any authenticated caller of the addGuests mutation to distinguish “booking does not exist” vs “booking exists but you lack permission,” which is a classic existence oracle for sequential integer booking IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — `replyTo: [organizer.email, ...attendees.map(({email}) => email)]` discloses the full attendee roster to team members never party to the booking [conf=50,P3]

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail sets `replyTo` to an array containing the organizer email plus **all attendee emails**: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), this organizer email is sent not only to the organizer but also to each `calendarEvent.team.members` via `new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent, teamMember })`. Those team members are recipients (`to`) and will receive an email whose Reply-To header includes the full attendee roster, which is a concrete privacy disclosure introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — no `booking.status`/`endTime` guard, so guests added to a CANCELLED/REJECTED/past booking receive an ICS with `method: "REQUEST"`/`status: "CONFIRMED"` that resurrects the dead meeting on their calendar [conf=100,P1]

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking is fetched and then unconditionally updated (attendees.createMany) and a CalendarEvent is built from booking.startTime/endTime without any checks against booking cancellation/rejection status or whether endTime is in the past. It then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests), and the newly added email templates generate ICS payloads with `method: "REQUEST"` and `status: "CONFIRMED"` regardless of the booking’s actual lifecycle state. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — attendee rows commit before `updateCalendarAttendees` with no transaction, compensating delete, or retry, so a provider failure leaves the DB permanently ahead of the external invite and retry is blocked by the dedupe check [conf=75,P1]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before calling the external side-effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no surrounding transaction, rollback/compensating delete, or retry strategy. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (provider/API failure), the handler will fail after the DB write, leaving attendees permanently added in the DB while the calendar provider was not updated. On a subsequent retry with the same guest emails, `uniqueGuests` will be filtered against the now-updated `booking.attendees` and become empty, triggering `BAD_REQUEST`, effectively blocking retry for the same guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — read-then-write dedupe against a line-26 snapshot with `createMany` and no `skipDuplicates` and no unique constraint, so concurrent/double-clicked mutations insert duplicates that no removeGuest path can undo [conf=75,P2]
